answer: An agent marketplace assigns voting weight to tokens locked for 30 days, rather than to account count. If an attacker splits 1,000 tokens among agents named sonnet, raven, and reef, their combined weight stays 1,000; creating more identities adds no influence. To control more votes, the attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, bearing the purchase cost, price risk, and loss of access to that capital during the lock.
